answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by requiring each agent to lock a bond that is slashed if it misbehaves. Creating thousands of fake identities becomes expensive because every duplicate must fund its own stake. A cheap impostor writing promises with a borrowed quill cannot hide: its funds flow through a narrow inlet watched by the network, and a failed audit leaves only a whisper of credibility. Genuine agents build reputation that compounds over time, while sybils bleed capital and vanish. The result is an identity system where honesty is cheaper than forgery.
